sentences.text: Odoribacter was proposed as a new genus in the family 'Porphyromonadaceae' when Bacteroides splanchnicus was reclassified as Odoribacter splanchnicus.
Odoribacter laneus was described from a strain isolated from human faeces, and Odoribacter splanchnicus is described as an anaerobe that normally inhabits the human intestine.
A review describes Odoribacter splanchnicus as widely present in the mammalian gut and able to synthesise metabolites, especially short-chain fatty acids.
That review reports that changes in its abundance have been correlated, positively or negatively, with obesity, metabolic syndrome, diabetes and intestinal inflammation.
Bloodstream infection with this species is reported to be rare; one report detected five cases of Odoribacter splanchnicus bacteraemia in a single laboratory over 2014-2024.
